sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 of the Sanborn Audubon series of August 1930, titled West Collingswood Heights, Haddon Township, Camden County. North is towards the upper right. The sheet covers the subdivision west of Black Horse Pike (also lettered Mt. Ephraim Pike), whose centre carries the boundary between Haddon Township and the Borough of Audubon along the right edge. Long, narrow blocks run from the upper left to the lower right between Marlboro Avenue, West Nicholson Road, Wilson, Lincoln, Washington, Grant and Marshall Avenues, crossed by New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania Avenues; west of New Jersey Avenue the rows of lots are offset from those to the east. Most lots are still vacant, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages. Buildings of note are the West Collingswood Heights Fire Co. No. 1 on Pennsylvania Avenue near West Nicholson Road, a club on the block south of Marlboro Avenue, an auto repair shop with a gasoline station facing the pike, a few stores along the pike, and the Haddon Lake Inn at the pike by the lake. Across the lower part of the sheet runs an abandoned railroad right of way. Below it Main Street, Tomasina and Lake Drive serve a few small blocks on the shore of Mt. Ephraim Lake, which with the South Branch of Newton Creek fills the lower left; the boundary between Haddon Township and Centre Township crosses the lake. The left margin carries a compass rose and the scale bar; the sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Marlboro Avenue is Marlborough Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Main is Main Street; Tomasina is Tomasina Avenue; Lake Drive is probably today's Lake Avenue (its junction with Tomasina Avenue fits within 2 m).

New Jersey Avenue was left out of the control: its junctions sit 6 to 7 m east of where New York Avenue, Pennsylvania Avenue and the pike put them, so the drawn street and the modern one do not coincide.
Two streets are lettered Marshall Avenue: one west of New Jersey Avenue by the creek and one east of it.
An abandoned railroad right of way crosses the sheet south of the residential blocks.
West Collingswood Heights Fire Co. No. 1 and the Haddon Lake Inn are drawn on this sheet.

Printed sheet 20 of the Audubon series (Aug. 1930): West Collingswood Heights, Haddon Township, west of Black Horse Pike (Mt. Ephraim Pike) at the Audubon line, about 39.892 N, 75.094 W. The catalog box (shared with West Berlin) was wrong; reference refetched. Scale 100 ft to an inch; north to the upper right (rotation about +18 deg). One part, mask null. New Jersey Av left out: its junctions sit 6 to 7 m east of where New York Av, Pennsylvania Av and the pike put them.
